raw.assessment: The incumbent provides embedded-caption previews and accessible history, consistent with final-format and retention needs. Twenty of 30 sessions met the time target, below the required 27; four downloads differed from expected captions, including one video-cut mismatch. Multiple saves, completion reversals and incomplete pairing records support a version-identification hypothesis, but do not establish whether errors arose during input binding or preview selection. H1-O7 limits a blanket rendering explanation: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes without uncertainty. Waiting and interpretation time remain unseparated, and festival capacity is unknown.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an immutable render-request record binding exact video and caption bytes, with the same identity visible when requesting and downloading, reduces unintended version combinations and selection errors.
openings.delta: Connect editor intent, worker inputs and delivered preview through one identity instead of independently named captions and completion-numbered previews.
openings.prediction: If input binding is faulty, worker hashes will differ from the confirmed request pair; if selection is faulty, hashes will agree but the downloaded request will differ from the intended one. Visible identities should reduce the latter.
openings.probe: On private staging, use fabricated footage to exercise overlapping requests and reversed completion. Have editors confirm each intended pair; compare that record with worker hashes and downloaded identity. Preserve the delivered pair and original caption bytes separately from draft selection.
assumptions: Input snapshots and identity display fit the four engineer-days and current private storage.
Editors can recognize the displayed pair within the one editor-day allocation.

openings.claim: Does obsolete render work, rather than preview interpretation, account for the missed time target?
openings.delta: Test whether coalescing pending draft requests could improve turnaround while retaining full embedded-caption rendering and delivered history.
openings.prediction: A queue bottleneck predicts delayed final-request starts behind obsolete work; an interpretation bottleneck predicts intended previews finishing promptly but being identified late.
openings.probe: Join render timestamps to staged editor selection and viewing timestamps. Replay observed request sequences with pending obsolete jobs omitted, preserving running jobs and delivered artifacts. Estimate processing savings before implementing coalescing.
assumptions: Timing capture and replay fit the shared engineering, editor and processing budgets.
Replay cannot establish unmeasured festival demand.

raw.assessment: The supplied observations establish delays and unexpected source versions, but do not separate rendering, selection, and viewing costs. The following capabilities are hypotheses; neither is established as sufficient within the available effort or computing allowance.

openings.claim: A private browser preview could immediately play the intended video with the latest explicitly selected caption snapshot, displaying one immutable identity for that pair; final delivery would still render embedded captions in the required format.
openings.delta: Separate caption audition from full rendering. Dependencies are private video playback, timestamped caption composition, immutable source snapshots, clear pair selection, and agreement between audition and embedded output. A presently testable partial capability is playback of one fabricated video with two caption revisions and a persistent pair label, alongside its embedded render. Keep the last delivered video and original captions independently accessible.
openings.prediction: If rendering dominates delay and audition is faithful enough, editors will identify correct wording and timing sooner; disagreement with embedded output or unchanged completion times would weaken this mechanism.
openings.probe: On existing private staging, have the two editors inspect fabricated examples in both modes, including timing boundaries and a changed video cut. Record source identity, wording/timing discrepancies, and waiting versus choosing/watching time. Fit the partial trial within the stated effort; meter processing and retain embedded delivery. Only a subsequent 30-session check can establish the target of at least 27 timely correct previews and zero unintended pairings.
assumptions: Browser and embedded caption behavior can be compared meaningfully.
A small prototype fits four engineer-days and one editor-day.
Unmeasured festival demand does not justify assuming spare processing capacity.

openings.claim: Were unexpected captions already bound to the wrong video when rendering began, or did editors choose an internally correct but unintended completed preview?
openings.delta: Discriminate source-binding failure from selection failure before choosing which capability to implement.
openings.prediction: A mismatch between requested and worker-consumed source hashes supports binding failure; matching job/output hashes with a different editor-intended pair supports selection failure. Both may occur.
openings.probe: Within the same effort budget, reproduce reversed completion order using fabricated sources; record editor intent, requested pair, worker input hashes, output identity and chosen download. Check retained events only where those fields exist; missing fields leave the historical cause unresolved.
assumptions: Staging exposes or can cheaply record source hashes at job execution.
Reproduction distinguishes possible mechanisms without proving historical causation.

openings.claim: Bind immutable source bytes to one visible request/download identity; distinguish binding from selection failure.
openings.discriminator: Requested/worker hash mismatch indicates binding; matching hashes but unintended downloaded identity indicates selection. Both may occur.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints; snapshot/display effort remains unverified.
openings.probe: Stage reversed completions with fabricated sources; compare editor intent, request pair, worker hashes, output and download identity.
openings.uncertainty: Missing historical fields prevent attribution; reproduction proves possibilities only. Editors must recognize identities.

openings.claim: Coalescing obsolete pending requests may reduce waiting.
openings.discriminator: Late final-request starts support queue delay; prompt completion followed by late identification supports interpretation delay.
openings.fit: Preserves running jobs, embedded rendering and delivered history; budget fit assumed.
openings.probe: Join render and selection/viewing timestamps; replay sequences omitting obsolete pending jobs and estimate savings.
openings.uncertainty: Single-correction successes limit blanket rendering explanations; festival demand remains unknown.

openings.claim: Private browser audition of an explicitly selected caption snapshot could bypass preview renders while retaining embedded delivery.
openings.discriminator: Faster correct judgment with matching embedded wording/timing supports audition; discrepancies or unchanged times weaken it.
openings.fit: Uncertain prototype effort and playback/composition fidelity.
openings.probe: Two editors compare labeled fabricated video/two-revision audition against embedded output, including timing boundaries and changed cuts; separate waiting, choosing and watching.
openings.uncertainty: Requires private playback, immutable snapshots, recognizable pairing and faithful output agreement.

lineage.reason: Merged with A2; retains identity mechanism and causal test.
Merged with Z1; preserves historical attribution limits.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose first; select implementation from results. All probes share four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 processing hours/week, use existing private accounts, retain embedded delivery and access to last delivery/original captions. Meter processing. Synthetic observations establish no efficacy; subsequent 30 sessions must yield at least 27 timely correct previews and zero unintended pairings.
